summary: Round-1 pre-submission review of the new notes/sim10_ada_100k_baseline_20261110 harness at 7a727fd24 (base 5f18da747). The 100k harness is a faithful adaptation of the accepted 10k harness: runner.py, bulk_accounting.py, runtime.py, gpu_tests.py and run.sbatch are byte-for-byte equivalent to the 10k versions except for the intended changes (--events choices 1000/100000, stage directory name sim10-ada-100k-<jobid>, --time=01:00:00, job name). campaign.py keeps the exact matrix (two 1000-event pilots, then four 100k passes in stream order 1,2,2,1), one BD, 24 physical cores, single scheduler-assigned L40S via nvidia-smi UUID, FFB-only staging with size+SHA verification, run_owned process-group reaping, and finally-block stage removal with cleanup receipt. support.fixture() now binds to the accepted sample10_100k fixture: it requires acceptance.json accepted/event_count 100000/root, matches generation_sha256 across acceptance/files/verification receipts, re-hashes verification.json against acceptance.verification_sha256, uses manifest['plan'] (not 'schedule') with service==12 to derive 100000 timestamps and checks them against verification.timestamp_sha256, requires format sample10-v1, JF streams exactly [5..9] covering panels 0-31, and per-file owner/size/hash agreement with files.json; this matches the writer in mfx_expand10_100k_20261109/repeat.py (plan entries carry timestamp/service, streams carry stream/panels/files{bd,smd}). JF bytes in files.json sum to 335,820,951,264 (312.76 GiB), consistent with 100000 x 3,358,200 payload bytes and the five-stream staging estimate. audit.py mirrors the 10k audit with 100000 identities, 500k reads, 335,820,000,000 bytes, 1000 callbacks of 100, drain, KvikIO settings, placement, cold cache, NIC/idle brackets, and now additionally re-validates the build-configuration allow-list and resolves the receipt source path. ADA-08 is closed: prepare_runtime.validate_configs requires the mismatch set to equal exactly {'psana/meson.build': pr 4cd07821…, frozen 27ae0bce…} (hashes identical to the older build-config-diff.json one-line gpu/notes packaging exclusion), persists config_mismatches in the receipt, audit.py line 15 re-runs the check, and test_runtime_receipt.py covers accept plus missing/new/changed/absent-frozen rejections; submit.py is checked in and freezes both the reviewed harness and the PR source as detached worktrees before calling prepare(). ADA-09 is closed: prepare() records repo.resolve(strict=True), audit resolves the receipt source, runtime.identity already resolved, and test_symlink_source exercises a symlinked receipt source. Test count in validation.json (22) matches the committed tests (15 audit + 2 campaign + 5 receipt). Remaining items are non-blocking: BDS-02 orphan risk is amplified by 10x larger files and the 100k README omits the orphan-recovery note the 10k README had; submit.py omits --chdir so the launch record depends on the submitter's cwd; config/native comparisons still iterate only PR-tracked files so deletions relative to the frozen tree are invisible; no timing budget is written down for the 60-minute limit. GPU tests and all measured results are pending and nothing measured is approved here.

This is a pre-launch review only. GPU acceptance tests, staging duration, cold-gate behaviour on 73 GiB files, memory-cgroup interaction with ~626 GiB of staged page-cache traffic, and all measured rates are pending and are not approved here.

findings.evidence: Closed. validate_configs() (lines 12-17) fails unless the pr!=frozen set equals exactly {'psana/meson.build': {pr 4cd07821…, frozen 27ae0bce…}}, matching the hashes in notes/sim10_ada_baseline_20261110/build-config-diff.json; the receipt persists build_configurations and config_mismatches (line 41); audit.py line 15 re-validates; test_runtime_receipt.py covers accept and four reject cases; submit.py is checked in and runs prepare() on the frozen PR worktree before sbatch; README.md and scope.md disclose the one-line packaging-only difference. Residual: both the native-source loop (lines 24-29) and the config loop (lines 32-35) iterate only files tracked in the PR checkout, so a native source or configuration file that exists in the frozen build tree but was deleted in the PR is never compared or reported.
findings.requested_change: No change required before submission. Optional hardening for a later campaign: also walk the frozen source tree for the same suffixes/config names and record any file missing from the PR as a mismatch (fail-closed unless allow-listed).

findings.evidence: Closed. prepare() records repo.resolve(strict=True) as receipt['source'] (prepare_runtime.py line 20), audit.py resolves (Path(receipt['source'])/'psana/psana').resolve() before the is_relative_to/relative_to checks, runtime.identity() already resolves module paths, and test_audit.py::test_symlink_source passes a symlinked receipt source against real runtime paths.

Carried over and amplified by 10x larger inputs. On SIGTERM the handler (line 24) raises SystemExit in the main thread while it is inside `with ThreadPoolExecutor(...) as pool: pool.map(copy, items)`; the executor's __exit__ waits for in-flight shutil.copyfile/sha calls on files up to 73,460,605,434 bytes before the finally at line 66 can rmtree the stage. With --signal=B:TERM@120 the grace period can expire first and leave an orphan sim10-ada-100k-<jobid> directory (~313 GiB) on the owner's FFB path. The 10k README (notes/sim10_ada_baseline_20261110/README.md lines 102-105) documented this orphan-recovery step; the 100k README.md does not mention it, and the new scope.md has no timing budget for the 60-minute limit.
findings.requested_change: Before submission (documentation only): add to README.md the orphan-recovery note naming the FFB directory sim10-ada-100k-<jobid> and a rough timing budget for the 60-minute allocation (GPU tests, ~313 GiB copy plus ~313 GiB SHA read-back, pilots, four ~95-120 s passes, cleanup). Optional code hardening: copy in chunks and check a stop flag set by the SIGTERM handler, or shutdown(cancel_futures=True) before re-raising, so staging aborts promptly.

findings.evidence: The sbatch command pins node, exclusions, output/error paths, script and arguments but passes no --chdir. The 10k submission (notes/sim10_ada_baseline_20261110/submission.json) used --chdir to the frozen source worktree. Without it the job's working directory is the submitter's cwd; if that path is node-local or absent on sdfada016, slurmstepd falls back to /tmp with a warning. run.sbatch uses only absolute paths so correctness is unaffected, but the recorded launch command is then not self-contained.
findings.requested_change: Add '--chdir='+str(source) to the command list in submit.py so submission.json fully determines the job environment. Not required for correctness.
